classification.difficultyReason: Apply the taught limiting-value model, calibrate its constant, solve for a target content and evaluate the derivative using that same model.

content.prompt:
A sponge has a water content of 800 mL when fully saturated.

When the sponge is dried out and then placed back in water, it absorbs water at a rate proportional to how much water it still needs to reach full saturation.

A squeezed sponge has 200 mL of water.

After being placed back into the water, it has water content of 440 mL after 3 seconds.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find when the water content rises to 790 mL. Give your answer to 1 decimal place.

answer.short: $24.0\text{ s}$ after being placed back in water.
answer.worked:
Let $W$ be the water content in millilitres and $t$ the time in seconds after the sponge is placed back in water.

$$\begin{align*}
\frac{dW}{dt}&=k(W-800),\qquad k<0\\
W&=800+Ae^{kt}\\
200&=800+A\\
A&=-600
\end{align*}$$

Using $W(3)=440$:

$$\begin{align*}
440&=800-600e^{3k}\\
600e^{3k}&=360\\
e^{3k}&=\frac35\\
3k&=\ln\left(\frac35\right)\\
k&=\frac{\ln(3/5)}3
\end{align*}$$

Thus $W=800-600e^{[\ln(3/5)/3]t}$. For $W=790$:

$$\begin{align*}
790&=800-600e^{kt}\\
600e^{kt}&=10\\
e^{kt}&=\frac1{60}\\
kt&=\ln\left(\frac1{60}\right)\\
t&=\frac{\ln(1/60)}k\\
t&=\frac{3\ln(1/60)}{\ln(3/5)}\\
t&\approx24.0\text{ s}.
\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the rate of absorption after 3 seconds. Give your answer to 1 decimal place.

answer.worked:
Using $W=800-600e^{kt}$ and $k=\dfrac{\ln(\frac{3}{5})}3$ from part a:

$$\begin{align*}
\frac{dW}{dt}&=-600ke^{kt}\\
\left.\frac{dW}{dt}\right|_{t=3}&=-600k\left(\frac35\right)\\
\left.\frac{dW}{dt}\right|_{t=3}&=-360\left(\frac{\ln(3/5)}3\right)\\
\left.\frac{dW}{dt}\right|_{t=3}&=-120\ln\left(\frac35\right)\\
\left.\frac{dW}{dt}\right|_{t=3}&\approx61.3\text{ mL/s}.
\end{align*}$$
